alternatives.text:
1.3 Automatic Subscription Renewal
All enterprise subscriptions renew automatically at the expiration of the active billing period to guarantee uninterrupted
service:
• Monthly Plans: Renew automatically every 30 days unless cancelled at least 48 hours prior to the next billing
   date.
• Annual Plans: Renew automatically for successive 12-month terms unless a written cancellation notice is received
   at least 30 calendar days prior to the annual contract expiration anniversary date.

3.1 Cancellation Submission Process
 Clients may initiate subscription cancellation via the CloudScale Admin Console (https://console.cloudscale.io/
 billing) or by emailing written notice to billing@cloudscale.io. Cancellation notices must be received at least 48
 hours prior to the next billing date.

3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
Downtime is defined as any continuous period of one (1) minute or more where covered platform services
are completely inaccessible across all availability zones, or where the HTTP server error rate (HTTP 5xx
responses) exceeds five percent (5.0%) across all valid customer API requests. The Monthly Uptime
Percentage is calculated using the following standard formula:
                                                                                             
                                       Total Scheduled Minutes in Month − Downtime Minutes
     Monthly Uptime Percentage =                                                                × 100
                                                   Total Scheduled Minutes in Month
Service availability is measured by automated synthetic probes executing health checks every sixty (60)
seconds from five external global regions (US-East, US-West, EU-Central, AP-East, and AU-Southeast).

Monthly Uptime %         Enterprise Credit       Professional Credit
                                                                        Application Mechanism
99.90% to < 99.99%        10% of Monthly Fee     SLA Target Met (0%)    Applied to subsequent billing invoice
99.00% to < 99.90%        25% of Monthly Fee      10% of Monthly Fee    Applied to subsequent billing invoice
98.00% to < 99.00%        50% of Monthly Fee      25% of Monthly Fee    Applied to subsequent billing invoice
95.00% to < 98.00%        50% of Monthly Fee      50% of Monthly Fee    Applied to subsequent billing invoice
< 95.00%                 100% of Monthly Fee     100% of Monthly Fee    Maximum allowable monthly credit
                      Table 2: Service Credit Compensation Brackets by Subscription Tier

4.3 Claim Submission Procedure and 30-Day Window
Customers must strictly follow this procedure to submit a service credit claim:
1. Filing Window: Claims must be submitted within thirty (30) calendar days following the end of the
   calendar month during which downtime occurred. Claims filed after 30 calendar days are permanently
   forfeited.
2. Submission Channel: Claims must be submitted via email to billing-credits@cloudscale.io or
   through the CloudScale billing portal ticket system.
3. Required Documentation: Claims must include: (a) Account ID and Organization Name; (b) exact
   dates, start times, and duration of the outage; (c) specific impacted service endpoints; and (d) customer-side
   error logs or traceroute data.

4.4 Credit Rules and Maximum Limitations
• Monthly Cap: Total service credits issued in any single calendar month shall not exceed 100% of the
   customer’s monthly recurring fee for that month.
• Non-Refundable: Service credits cannot be exchanged for cash refunds, wire transfers, or credit card
  chargebacks.
• Sole Financial Remedy: Service credits constitute the customer’s sole and exclusive financial remedy
  for downtime.

expected_database_response.reference_sql:
SELECT c.customer_id, c.company_name, c.tier, c.region,
       c.status AS account_status, s.subscription_id,
       s.billing_cycle, s.monthly_rate, s.start_date, s.renewal_date,
       s.payment_status, i.ticket_id, i.severity, i.downtime_minutes,
       i.reported_at, i.resolved_at, i.status AS incident_status,
       i.sla_breached
FROM customers AS c
JOIN subscriptions AS s ON s.customer_id = c.customer_id
LEFT JOIN incident_tickets AS i
  ON i.customer_id = c.customer_id
 AND substr(i.reported_at, 1, 7) = :month
WHERE c.company_name = :company_name
ORDER BY s.subscription_id, i.ticket_id;

database_results.sql:
SELECT c.company_name, c.tier, c.region, s.plan_name, s.billing_cycle, s.monthly_rate, s.start_date, s.renewal_date, GROUP_CONCAT(i.ticket_id || '|' || i.downtime_minutes || '|' || i.reported_at || '|' || i.resolved_at || '|' || i.status || '|' || i.sla_breached) AS tickets
FROM customers c
JOIN subscriptions s ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
LEFT JOIN incident_tickets i ON c.customer_id = i.customer_id AND i.reported_at >= '2024-03-01' AND i.reported_at < '2024-04-01'
WHERE c.company_name = 'Zenith Cloud Robotics'
GROUP BY c.customer_id;

SELECT c.company_name, c.tier, c.region, s.plan_name, s.billing_cycle, s.monthly_rate, s.start_date, s.renewal_date, GROUP_CONCAT(i.ticket_id || '|' || i.downtime_minutes || '|' || i.reported_at || '|' || i.resolved_at || '|' || i.status || '|' || i.sla_breached) AS tickets
FROM customers c
JOIN subscriptions s ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
LEFT JOIN incident_tickets i ON c.customer_id = i.customer_id AND i.reported_at >= '2024-03-01' AND i.reported_at < '2024-04-01'
WHERE c.company_name = 'Zenith Cloud Robotics'
GROUP BY c.customer_id;

### 1.2 Subscription Cycles and Billing Options

CloudScale offers two recurring subscription billing options for enterprise accounts:

- Monthly Billing Cycle: Subscriptions are invoiced every 30 calendar days in advance. This option provides operational agility with no long-term contractual commitment.
- Annual Billing Cycle: Subscriptions are prepaid in advance for a continuous 12-month period. Clients selecting the annual billing cycle receive an immediate 15% upfront discount relative to standard monthly rates across all compute tiers and base platform licenses.

retrieved_document_chunks.text:
### 3.3 Scheduled Maintenance Policy

Maintenance is required to apply security patches, upgrade operating systems, and perform hardware maintenance:

- Advance Notice Period: CloudScale will provide a mandatory minimum of forty-eight (48) hours advance written notice prior to any scheduled maintenance. Notice is published on the status portal (https://status.cloudscale.io) and emailed to account administrators.
- Standard Window: Scheduled maintenance is conducted during off-peak hours on Sundays between 01:00 UTC and 05:00 UTC.
- Monthly Cap: Scheduled maintenance shall not exceed four (4) cumulative hours in any single calendar month. Any maintenance beyond 4 hours, or conducted without 48 hours notice, counts as Downtime.
- Emergency Maintenance: In critical situations (e.g., zero-day security vulnerabilities), CloudScale may conduct emergency maintenance with at least one (1) hour advance notice or immediate post-incident notice.

### 1.1 Covered Services (In-Scope Components)

This SLA governs the operational uptime, availability, and technical support for three core platform systems:

1. Cloud Infrastructure: Scalable virtual compute instances, software-defined virtual private clouds (VPCs), edge load balancers, persistent block storage volumes, and distributed object storage.
2. Managed Database Engine: High-availability managed PostgreSQL clusters and distributed cache nodes, including automated failover, cluster synchronization, and continuous transactional backups.
3. CloudScale API Platform: Public REST API endpoints, GraphQL queries and mutations, incoming/outgoing webhook dispatch engines, and customer identity/authentication microservices.

### 4.3 Claim Submission Procedure and 30-Day Window

Customers must strictly follow this procedure to submit a service credit claim:

1. Filing Window: Claims must be submitted within thirty (30) calendar days following the end of the calendar month during which downtime occurred. Claims filed after 30 calendar days are permanently forfeited.
2. Submission Channel: Claims must be submitted via email to billing-credits@cloudscale.io or through the CloudScale billing portal ticket system.
3. Required Documentation: Claims must include: (a) Account ID and Organization Name; (b) exact dates, start times, and duration of the outage; (c) specific impacted service endpoints; and (d) customer-side error logs or traceroute data.

### 3.1 Cancellation Submission Process

Clients may initiate subscription cancellation via the CloudScale Admin Console (https://console.cloudscale.io/ billing) or by emailing written notice to billing@cloudscale.io. Cancellation notices must be received at least 48 hours prior to the next billing date.

retrieved_document_chunks.section: 3. Cancellation & Refund Windows / 3.2 Annual Plans: 14-Day Money-Back Guarantee
retrieved_document_chunks.text:
### 3.2 Annual Plans: 14-Day Money-Back Guarantee

CloudScale provides a 14-day money-back guarantee for annual enterprise plans, subject to two strict requirements:

- Submission Window: The refund request must be delivered in writing within 14 calendar days of the initial service activation date.
- Usage Limit Requirement: Total compute usage during the initial 14-day window must remain under 50 computing hours. If telemetry logs show 50 or more computing hours consumed, the annual subscription becomes strictly non-refundable.
- Post-14-Day Cancellations: Requests submitted after the 14-day window are non-refundable. Platform access continues until the end of the paid 12-month term.

### 4.1 Eligibility Overview & Starter Exclusion

If CloudScale fails to meet its monthly uptime commitment, eligible customers may request a Service Credit. Service Credits represent a percentage discount credited against future monthly invoices.

Starter Tier Exclusion: The Starter tier is expressly excluded from receiving service credits. Starter tier customers receive 0% service credits under all circumstances.

retrieved_document_chunks.header_path: 6. Exclusions & Limitations
retrieved_document_chunks.section: 6. Exclusions & Limitations
retrieved_document_chunks.text:
## 6. Exclusions & Limitations

The following circumstances are expressly excluded from the calculation of Downtime and are not eligible for Service Credits:

1. Client Misconfigurations: Unavailability caused by client configuration errors, invalid custom code, improper database queries, customer firewall misconfigurations, or expired SSL/TLS certificates uploaded by the client.
2. Unauthorized Modifications: System disruptions resulting from customer actions that violate CloudScale documentation, unapproved administrative overrides, or unsupported third-party software installations.
3. Third-Party Internet & External Outages: Outages caused by external internet service providers (ISPs), public BGP routing disruptions, upstream transit carrier failures, or client telecommunication lines outside CloudScale's core data center edge.
4. Force Majeure Events: Unforeseeable events beyond CloudScale's reasonable control, including natural catastrophes (floods, earthquakes, severe storms), war, civil disturbance, national electrical grid failure, or government sanctions.
5. Beta & Pre-Release Services: Features, APIs, or products explicitly designated as "Beta", "Preview", "Experimental", or "Early Access", which are offered "as-is" without performance guarantees.
6. Resource Quota Violations & Rate Throttling: Service degradation or rejected requests resulting from customer traffic exceeding agreed contractual quotas or unthrottled client loops triggering automated rate limiters.
7. Properly Announced Scheduled Maintenance: Maintenance executed within designated windows adhering to the mandatory 48-hour advance notification requirement.
8. Account Suspensions: Outages caused by account suspension or termination due to overdue unpaid invoices or material violations of CloudScale's Acceptable Use Policy (AUP).

retrieved_document_chunks.section: 5. Support Incident Severity Levels & Response Times / 5.1 Incident Severity Definitions
retrieved_document_chunks.text:
### 5.1 Incident Severity Definitions

CloudScale categorizes technical support incidents into four clearly defined severity categories:

- Severity 1 (Critical): Complete production outage, total loss of database services, or primary API failure affecting all end-users. No workaround exists. Critical business operations are completely halted.
- Severity 2 (Major): Core platform functionality is significantly degraded, API latency increases > 300% over baseline, or high-volume transactional flows are impaired. Limited workarounds exist, but throughput is degraded.
- Severity 3 (Minor): Non-critical software defects, localized errors affecting minor endpoints, or cosmetic portal bugs. Production systems remain operational without material impairment.
- Severity 4 (General Guidance): Administrative questions, setup guidance, documentation inquiries, or enhancement requests. Zero impact on production systems.

retrieved_document_chunks.text:
## 2. Subscription Tiers

CloudScale offers three subscription tiers designed to match different workload maturity, scalability, and operational support requirements:

- Starter Tier: Created for individual developers, sandbox testing, and non-production proofs of concept. Services operate on shared multi-tenant cluster infrastructure. Support is self-service via community forums and public documentation. Starter tier accounts receive no uptime guarantees, have no response time SLAs, and are entirely excluded from service credit eligibility.
- Professional Tier: Engineered for growing commercial businesses, standard production web platforms, and operational SaaS workloads. Includes dedicated multi-availability zone (Multi-AZ) virtual compute resources, automated daily database snapshots, standard business-hours technical support, 24/7 on-call coverage for critical outages, and eligibility for financial service credits if availability targets are missed.
- Enterprise Tier: Architected for mission-critical enterprise systems requiring continuous availability, massive throughput, and stringent operational governance. Includes isolated single-tenant or multi-region architecture, continuous point-in-time database recovery (PITR with 1-second recovery point objective), a designated Technical Account Manager (TAM), 24/7/365 priority hotline and Slack support, and our highest availability commitment of 99.99% uptime.

### 3.1 Monthly Availability Commitments

CloudScale measures service availability monthly across each calendar month. The uptime target represents the percentage of scheduled minutes during which covered services remain reachable, responsive, and error-free.

Table 1: Service Availability Commitments and Maximum Allowable Monthly Downtime

| Subscription Tier   | Monthly Uptime Target   | Max Allowed Downtime (30-day mo.)   | High- Availability Architecture       |
|---------------------|-------------------------|-------------------------------------|---------------------------------------|
| Starter             | 99.00%                  | 7 hours, 12 minutes (432.0 min)     | Shared cluster infrastructure         |
| Professional        | 99.90%                  | 43 minutes, 12 seconds (43.2 min)   | High- availability Multi-AZ clus- ter |
| Enterprise          | 99.99%                  | 4 minutes, 19 seconds (4.32 min)    | Multi-Region active-active failover   |
